passages.context: A Lapide reports that the Syriac and Greek end-subscriptions, Jerome, Athanasius's Synopsis, Theodoret's Pauline preface, and others assign Galatians to Rome. He immediately reports that Chrysostom and Baronius deny Rome and place it before Romans, at Ephesus or another Greek city; he then concludes that neither the epistle nor other evidence permits a certain determination of its time or place and calls it, in that respect, the most uncertain of Paul's letters.
passages.notes: Read directly on printed p. 457, artifact PDF p. 514. This passage supports a faithful report of the Roman subscription-and-patristic tradition together with a Lapide's preserved countertradition and explicit uncertainty. It does not support 'a Lapide teaches Rome,' a unanimous patristic claim, or independent verification here of each earlier author he names.

passages.context: Within the general proemium's numbered ordering of Paul's letters, the sixth entry dates Galatians to AD 58. The chronological series concludes by identifying Baronius as its source. This passage therefore controls the statement 'AD 58 in the Baronius-based chronology reproduced by a Lapide,' not an unqualified modern date or a claim that a Lapide independently derived the year.
passages.notes: Read directly on printed p. 19, artifact PDF p. 31. The sixth entry supplies a year but no place of composition; any place claim requires a distinct source locus.

work.author: Cornelius a Lapide
work.description: Cornelius a Lapide's Catholic commentary on the Pauline epistles. Its general proemium treats Pauline chronology and order; each epistle is introduced by its own argumentum before the verse-by-verse exposition.
